question.text: As per the SEBI PFUTP Regulations, 2003, circular transactions in respect of a security entered into between persons including intermediaries are prohibited if they are intended to:

answer.text: Artificially provide a false appearance of trading or to inflate, depress or cause fluctuations in the price of the security
Only inflate the price of the security
Transfer beneficial ownership between connected parties
Only provide a false appearance of trading

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 4(2)(k) prohibits circular transactions in respect of a security entered into between persons including intermediaries that are intended to artificially provide a false appearance of trading in the security, or to inflate, depress, or cause fluctuations in its price. The Trap: The "only inflate the price" and "only provide a false appearance of trading" options are each partial — they capture only one limb of Regulation 4(2)(k) and miss the combined false-appearance + price-manipulation test. Note: The Regulation 4(2)(k) wording above is the only point directly grounded in the checked Series III-A workbook pages.
